partners.diseaseBName: glycogen storage disease due to glycogen branching enzyme deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: GYS2 (HGNC:4499) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen Synthesis (GO:0005985); Glycogen Synthesis (GO:0005985) —DECREASES→ Abnormal Glycogen (reduced branching/size) (CHEBI:17147); Abnormal Glycogen (reduced branching/size) (CHEBI:17147) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0000764); GBE1 (HGNC:4129) —DISRUPTS→ Glycogen Branching (GO:0004066); Glycogen Branching (GO:0004066) —DECREASES→ Abnormal Glycogen (excessively long chains) (CHEBI:17147); Abnormal Glycogen (excessively long chains) (CHEBI:17147) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0003124). Deficiency in GYS2 (Disease A) disrupts normal glycogen synthesis, leading to abnormal glycogen structures and cellular dysfunction manifesting as hepatomegaly. Deficiency in GBE1 (Disease B) disrupts glycogen branching, resulting in the accumulation of long, unbranched glycogen chains that also impair cellular function, leading to hypoglycemia. Both disruptions converge on abnormal glycogen metabolism and storage, impacting cellular homeostasis and leading to distinct but related clinical presentations.

partners.diseaseBName: glycogen storage disease due to muscle and heart glycogen synthase deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: GYS2 (HGNC:4534) —DISRUPTS→ glycogen synthesis (GO:0005971); GYS1 (HGNC:4533) —DISRUPTS→ glycogen synthesis (GO:0005971); glycogen synthesis (GO:0005971) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001250); glycogen synthesis (GO:0005971) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); glycogen synthesis (GO:0005971) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324). Loss-of-function mutations in GYS2 (hepatic glycogen synthase) disrupt hepatic glycogen synthesis, leading to hypoglycemia (Disease A). Loss-of-function mutations in GYS1 (muscle and heart glycogen synthase) disrupt glycogen synthesis in muscle and heart, leading to cardiomyopathy and muscle weakness (Disease B). Both GYS1 and GYS2 are essential for the shared pathway of glycogen synthesis, which, when disrupted, leads to distinct but related phenotypes.

partners.mechanism_chain: GYS2 (HGNC:4553) —DISRUPTS→ hepatic glycogen metabolism (GO:0005977); hepatic glycogen metabolism (GO:0005977) —DECREASES→ glycogen (CHEBI:17077); glycogen (CHEBI:17077) —LEADS_TO→ hepatic dysfunction (HP:0001393); EPM2A (HGNC:3225) —DISRUPTS→ lysosomal degradation of glycogen aggregates (GO:0000283); lysosomal degradation of glycogen aggregates (GO:0000283) —LEADS_TO→ myoclonic epilepsy (HP:0001274). Loss-of-function mutations in GYS2 impair hepatic glycogen synthesis, leading to glycogen storage disorder and hepatic dysfunction. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in EPM2A impair the lysosomal degradation of abnormal glycogen aggregates (Lafora bodies), causing myoclonic epilepsy. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of glycogen metabolism allows for the exploration of common therapeutic strategies targeting glycogen breakdown or cellular detoxification pathways.
